title: HachiFI: A Lightweight SoC Architecture-Independent Fault-Injection Framework for SEU Impact Evaluation
problem: Evaluating reliability of electronic devices under Single-Event Upsets (SEUs) triggered by energetic particles in safety-critical applications. Traditional irradiation experiments are costly; prior fault injection lacks full coverage and accuracy.
motivation: Safety-critical deployment requires pre-deployment reliability assessment. SEU events cause unexpected bit-flips in memory/registers with significant system anomalies.
method: The framework automatically injects faults (simulated particle impacts) throughout a system by accessing memory and scan chains—built-in testing pathways—to cover 100% of potential failure points. It simulates particle-induced bit flips based on measured cross-sections, the probability of impact at different particle energies, and supports both system-wide and component-level testing. The approach works across any processor architecture and adds only about 2% computational overhead.
key_novelty: Complete fault injection coverage (100% of all possible bit flips) is achieved through direct hardware access with minimal performance overhead (<2%) while matching real particle irradiation with 98.4% correlation.
contributions: 100% coverage fault injection framework independent of SoC architecture
Sub-2% hardware overhead for complete SEU simulation
Validated on 22nm edge-AI chip showing 0.984 R² match to irradiation
limitations: Validation limited to 22nm technology; scalability and applicability to other process nodes not discussed.
